references.text: Both texts deal with staying outside the camp due to impurity and illustrate the principle of separating the unclean from the clean in Israel's camp.
This text gives a command to send unclean persons outside the camp, which aligns with the principle of having a designated place outside the camp for unclean purposes.
Here soldiers who have killed or touched a dead body are commanded to stay outside the camp for seven days, showing the same principle of separation from the camp for purity.
The leper shall live outside the camp during their period of impurity, illustrating the same principle of staying outside the camp for reasons of cleansing.
Hebrews refers to Jesus suffering outside the city gate and encourages believers to go out to him outside the camp, as a spiritual application of this principle.
